sections.label: Green plan and green skills
sections.summary: The Government released the Singapore Green Plan 2030, launched GFIT initiatives, completed a carbon services hub study, and SkillsFuture Singapore identified green job roles and training courses.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Since that debate, the Government had released the Singapore Green Plan 2030, launched new initiatives by the Green Finance Industry Taskforce (GFIT) and completed a study on establishing Singapore as a carbon services hub.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Last month, in the inaugural Skills Demand for the Future Economy report, SkillsFuture Singapore identified job roles requiring green skills and curated the corresponding training courses.

sections.label: Manufacturing share of GDP
sections.summary: Manufacturing contributes 21% to GDP, the largest sector by share, and employs almost half a million workers.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Manufacturing contributes 21% to our GDP, the largest sector by share and employs almost half a million workers.

sections.label: Jurong Island transformation
sections.summary: Jurong Island oil hub will be transformed into an energy and chemicals park that operates sustainably.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
sentences.text: For instance, Jurong Island oil hub will be transformed into an energy and chemicals park that operates sustainably.

sections.label: Solar energy share in 2030
sections.summary: Solar energy will only meet about 3% of total electricity demand in 2030 despite more solar panels on rooftops and reservoirs.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Even as we step up the installation of solar panels on rooftops and over water reservoirs, the solar energy we make will only meet about 3% of our total electricity demand in 2030.

sections.label: Low-carbon electricity by 2035
sections.summary: If all goes well, around 30% of electricity will come from low-carbon sources by 2035.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
sentences.text: If all goes well, we will get around 30% of our electricity from low-carbon sources by 2035.

sections.label: Malaysia renewable energy targets
sections.summary: Malaysia plans to raise renewable energy to 31% of installed capacity in 2025 and 40% in 2035 under its power generation plan.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Similarly, Malaysia plans to increase the share of renewable energy in its installed capacity to 31% in 2025 and 40% in 2035 under its power generation plan.

sections.label: Carbon trading and renewable energy
sections.summary: This states that international carbon trading agreed at COP26 can offset emissions and access neighbouring countries' renewable energy to meet carbon commitments.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
sentences.text: This gives us a way out of our severe constraints in alternative energy.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
sentences.text: It means that we can use the international carbon trading framework as agreed at COP26, to purchase and offset our emissions, and tap into renewable energy positive resources in our neighbouring countries to meet our global carbon commitment.

sections.label: Green job roles report
sections.summary: The inaugural Skills Demand for the Future Economy report identified over 450 green job roles across 17 sectors.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
sentences.text: The inaugural Skills Demand for the Future Economy report has identified more than 450 green job roles across 17 sectors, ranging from manufacturing and trade and connectivity, to financial services and the built environment.

sections.label: S$180 million programme support
sections.summary: S$180 million is set aside to support at least 6,000 companies for training workshops, capability and product development projects, certification and financing.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
sentences.text: The S$180 million set aside for the programme aims to support at least 6,000 companies for training workshops, capability and product development projects, and key enablers such as certification and financing.

sections.label: Sustainability centre for SMEs
sections.summary: The Sustainability Experience Centre for SMEs at Nanyang Polytechnic is cited as an example of measures to guide SMEs' green transformation.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
sentences.text: The Sustainability Experience Centre for SMEs sited at Nanyang Polytechnic is a good example of measures to reach out to SMEs and guide them with the green transformation of their operations.

sections.label: Swappable batteries for electric bikes
sections.summary: A network of shared swappable batteries for electric bikes is described as convenient and efficient, with Gogoro implemented in Taiwan and Israel and rolling out in Chinese and Indian cities.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
sentences.text: For example, a network of shared and swappable batteries for electric bikes distributed across the island can be a convenient and efficient option vis-à-vis EV chargers solution.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Such swappable batteries solutions such as Gogoro are already implemented in Taiwan and Israel and will be rolled out in Chinese and Indian cities this year.

sections.label: Coordinated team for green transition
sections.summary: This calls for the Government, civil society groups and the community to work as a coordinated team to develop a low-carbon green ecosystem.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
sentences.text: On the other, we also need to sustain this transition over the long term.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Most importantly, we must work together as a closely coordinated team, comprising the Government, civil society groups and the community, to develop a low-carbon and green ecosystem.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
sentences.text: We hope to have the support of this House and Singaporeans to press ahead on this green journey together, to build a better Singapore for our future generations.

sections.label: Record wildfires, heat, floods
sections.summary: Regions from California to Siberia faced record wildfires, the Arctic hit 38 degrees Celsius, and catastrophic floods struck India, Europe, Malaysia, Australia and China.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Regions, from sunny California to snowy Siberia, faced their largest wildfires in history.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The Arctic hit a record high of 38 degree Celsius.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Catastrophic floods struck India, Europe, Malaysia, Australia and China.

sections.label: US extreme winter weather toll
sections.summary: Extreme winter weather left nearly 10 million people in the US without power and water, killed 318 people and caused nearly US$200 billion of damage.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Extreme winter weather left nearly 10 million people in the US without power and water.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: It killed 318 people and caused nearly US$200 billion of damage, making it the deadliest and costliest natural disaster in US history.

sections.label: Three net zero proposals
sections.summary: Three proposals: commit to net zero emissions by 2050, raise the carbon tax to a price needed for net zero, and expand carbon tax coverage to all reportable facilities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: In this spirit, I come to this House with three proposals: first, we should commit to achieving net zero emissions by 2050; second, we should increase the carbon tax to a price necessary to achieve net zero emissions by 2050; and third, we should expand coverage of the carbon tax to include all reportable facilities.

sections.label: Singapore net zero commitment
sections.summary: Singapore's current commitment is to reach net zero as soon as possible after 2050.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Singapore’s current commitment is to reach net zero as soon as possible after 2050.

sections.label: Carbon tax rate and potential
sections.summary: The carbon tax has the highest potential to reshape incentives and motivate action, but the current rate is $5 per tonne.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: But the carbon tax has the highest potential to reshape incentives and motivate action.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: But our current rate is $5 per tonne.

sections.label: Carbon tax facility threshold
sections.summary: The carbon tax currently applies only to facilities emitting at least 25 kilotonnes of CO2-equivalent in a year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Currently, carbon tax applies only to facilities emitting at least 25 kilotonnes of CO2-equivalent in a year.

sections.label: Government green bond financing
sections.summary: The Government can mandate statutory boards to issue green bonds and set green financing rules, building on MAS' Greenprint initiative.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: The Government can lead the way to promote sustainable financing by mandating its statutory boards, like MAS, LTA, HDB and NEA, to issue green bonds and laying the framework and rules for green financing.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: This is on top of the S$19 billion worth of selected public infrastructure projects identified to be financed by green bonds.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: I hope our government can commit to a minimum number of green bond issuances every year, including a standalone retail green bond product which can be tied to the country's sovereign rating, so as to broaden the pool of Singaporean green investors.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: The Government may consider reporting on the social benefits of expenditures financed by green bonds financing, such as job creation, access to affordable infrastructure and socio-economic advancement.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: We can build on MAS’ Greenprint initiative and formulate a Singapore Green Financing framework which sets out the Government’s environmental agenda and its vision for enhancing Singapore’s leadership as the Asia’s green financial centre.

sections.label: ISCA accountancy body membership
sections.summary: ISCA is the national accountancy body with more than 33,000 professional accountants as members.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: ISCA is the national accountancy body which has more than 33,000 professional accountants as its members.

sections.label: Sustainability courses for accountants
sections.summary: ISCA will roll out sustainability courses and certification programmes, with training grants and funding from Government agencies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Given that sustainability is a new growth area and to equip Singapore Chartered Accountants with the necessary skill sets to flourish in this area, ISCA will be rolling out courses and certification programmes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: In development of such upskilling programmes, there will be significant content development involved.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: And to encourage more professional accountants to upskill and perform higher value roles, training grants can be made available to encourage employers to send their staff for training.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: In this area, Government agencies such as Accounting and Corporate Regulatory Authority, Singapore Accountancy Commission and SkillsFuture can provide funding and grants to ease development costs and offset training expenses.

sections.label: Carbon tax electricity price impact
sections.summary: Every $5 per tonne of carbon tax could lead to approximately 1% increase in electricity prices for households and businesses.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: In the case of carbon tax, it is estimated that every $5 per tonne of carbon tax could lead to approximately 1% increase in electricity prices for households and businesses in Singapore.

sections.label: Carbon tax spending and industry support
sections.summary: The Government is prepared to spend more than it collects from carbon taxes and is increasing funding support for industry energy efficiency.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: MSE Minister Grace Fu has indicated in an answer to a recent Parliamentary Question that the Government is prepared to spend more than it collects from carbon taxes on worthwhile projects that reduce carbon emissions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: In the same reply, the Minister also mentioned about increasing funding support to assist industries in improving energy and carbon efficiency by way of the Resource Efficiency Grant and the Energy Efficiency Fund (E2F).

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: The Government is also working with companies based on Jurong Island to transform the island into a sustainable energy and chemicals park, and to develop and export the low-carbon solutions globally.

sections.label: ASEAN green economy value
sections.summary: A 2020 Bain and Company report estimated ASEAN's green economy could be worth up to US$1 trillion annually by 2030.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: A 2020 report by Bain and Company has estimated that ASEAN's green economy could be worth up to US$1 trillion in annual economic benefits by 2030.

sections.label: Green economy job roles
sections.summary: The SkillsFuture inaugural report identified the green economy as a key growth area, with over 450 job roles in 17 sectors requiring green skills.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: The green economy was identified as a key growth area in the recent SkillsFuture inaugural report.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: It highlighted that today, there are more than 450 job roles in 17 sectors that require green skills, including manufacturing, financial services, trade and connectivity, hospitality, and the built environment.

sections.label: Pacing green transformation
sections.summary: It states the need to pace green transformation, support businesses, seize green economy opportunities, and equip the workforce with skills.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: To do so, we need to pace out our green transformation and support businesses in their journey, seize the green economy opportunities, and equip our workforce with the skills to take on the jobs in the green economy.

sections.label: Singapore low natural capital
sections.summary: Singapore reports extremely low natural capital, with $62 of $817,846 per capita wealth attributable to natural sources.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Unsurprisingly, Singapore reports extremely low levels of natural capital.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Of the $817,846 in per capita wealth, a miserly $62 was attributable to natural sources, both renewable and non-renewable.

sections.label: Green bonds programme offices
sections.summary: MOF established a Green Bonds Programme Office in September last year, and NEA became the first statutory board to issue medium-term notes under its Green Bond Framework.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: The MOF established a Green Bonds Programme Office in September last year.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: A month prior, NEA became the first statutory board to issue medium-term notes under its Green Bond Framework.

sections.label: Green bonds share of market
sections.summary: The estimated $500 billion in green bonds issued worldwide in 2021 is 0.4% of the $119 trillion global fixed income market.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: The estimated $500 billion in green bonds issued worldwide in 2021 is only a miniscule 0.4% of the $119 trillion global fixed income market.

sections.label: Recycling contamination and ESG ratings
sections.summary: Contamination renders an estimated 40% of recyclables unusable, a third of recyclables are exported, and ESG criteria may privilege social or governance over environmental factors.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: At best, this creates additional work for the conservancy contractors and at the sorting center; at worst, the contamination by food and liquid waste renders an estimated 40% of recyclables unusable.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: As of 2019, we continue to export a third of our recyclables, to an uncertain consummation.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Even as we enter into this market in earnest with our proposed exchanges, we need to guard against whether the ESG criteria are overly flexible, and, in particular, whether the ultimate rating ends up privileging the "social" or "governance" – the "S" and "G", respectively – rather than the environmental – the "E".

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: This has resulted in dubious players issuing bonds under the rubric of sustainability, including a number of clean coal projects in China that were sold by Spanish oil company Repsol.

sections.label: Greenwashing regulation and environmental audits
sections.summary: Speaker notes greenwashing regulation exists in several countries and asks about NGO collaboration and requiring environmental audits for listed or major-emitting firms.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Regulation over misleading environmental claims is currently practised in Australia, Canada, the European Union, Norway and United States, to varying degrees.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: To this end, I wonder if the Minister will be willing to elaborate on regulation specifically targeted at greenwashing and whether there are such existing collaborative efforts with NGOs to account for greenwashing risks in environmental labeling.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Simultaneously, we could promote and develop a private sector that undertakes environmental audits, perhaps by requiring that listed firms, or firms that are among the major emitters, regardless of size, routinely report such audits, much like how we require routine financial statement reporting, albeit in this case, perhaps, with lower frequency.

sections.label: MAS green finance initiatives
sections.summary: MAS launched the Green Finance Action Plan in 2019 and Project Greenprint in December 2020 to promote a green finance ecosystem.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: MAS launched the Green Finance Action Plan in 2019.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: The actions for six identified areas include setting Environmental Risk Management Guidelines for banking, insurance and asset management, grants for green loans through grants, committing US$2 billion to a Green Investments Programme, promoting fintech innovation, and supporting climate research and training.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: MAS followed up with Project Greenprint in December 2020 to promote a green finance ecosystem by using technology to mobilise capital, monitor sustainability commitments and measure impact.

sections.label: Carbon tax rate review
sections.summary: MOF announced it will review the carbon tax rate for 2024, expected to be higher than the previously announced $10-$15 range for 2030.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: MOF had announced that they will be reviewing the carbon tax rate for 2024 which is expected to be higher than the $10-$15 range previously announced for 2030.

sections.label: Just transition support
sections.summary: Speaker asks the Government to support a just transition in deeds, an idea advanced by the ILO.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: I will ask that this Government throws its support behind a just transition, not just in words, but also in deeds.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: This idea is advanced by the International Labour Organization (ILO) as a process towards an environmentally sustainable economy which needs to be well-managed and contribute to the goals of decent work for all, social inclusion and eradication of poverty.

sections.label: COP26 just transition declaration
sections.summary: Speaker asks the Government to review the COP26 just transition declaration and consider supporting the pledge and efforts.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: On words, I ask that the Government review the COP26 just transition declaration and consider supporting the said pledge and efforts, putting social dialogue as well as rights at work at the centre of policies for strong sustainable and inclusive growth and development for our workforce.

sections.label: Just transition roadmap for workers
sections.summary: Speaker cites ILO clause 29(b) and asks Ministries and Statutory Boards to work on a just transition roadmap for at-risk Singaporean workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: Clause 29(b) of the ILO's just transition guidelines also ask that governments, in consultation with social partners, and I quote, "Give particular attention to unemployed workers and workers at risk of unemployment in communities and industries affected by climate change, resource degradation or structural change, including those in the informal economy." We need to help Singaporean workers in sectors who are being affected or will soon be affected by developments in the green economy.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: We need to look at how to prepare Singaporean workers to go into jobs, which will be created in the green economy.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: Therefore, I ask that the relevant Ministries and Statutory Boards work on a just transition roadmap for Singaporean workers which can be at risk of displacement as the green economy develops.

sections.label: Just transition funding measures
sections.summary: The Workers' Party welcomed carbon taxes and said funding must channel carbon taxes to just transition measures, citing the EU's just transition mechanism.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: My Parliamentary colleague, Mr Gerald Giam, has previously called for extending the Special Employment Credit scheme to provide time-limited wage support to all Singaporeans workers while taking up their first job in the green economy.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: All these may require funding of course and the Workers' Party has welcomed carbon taxes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: However, we will need to consider funding mechanism to properly channel carbon taxes towards a just transition measures.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: Here, the Government can take reference from the EU's just transition mechanism, which includes a just transition fund offering financial supporting and technical assistance for most affected communities, such as low-income communities.

sections.label: Singapore carbon price comparison
sections.summary: Singapore's carbon pricing of S$5 per tonne falls far short of the IMF's guidance of US$75 or S$100 per tonne for advanced economies.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: Our current carbon pricing at the rate of S$5 per tonne of emissions pales in comparison to other jurisdictions, falling far short of the recent IMF’s guidance of US$75 or S$100 per tonne of emissions for advanced economies.

sections.label: Companies covered by carbon tax
sections.summary: The carbon tax applies to about 30 to 40 companies employing over 27,000 workers and constituting 3% of Singapore's GDP.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: Speaker, Sir, the carbon tax in Singapore applies to approximately 30 to 40 companies.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: These high emission firms such as power generation and petrochemicals directly employ over 27,000 workers and constitute 3% of Singapore’s GDP while providing business activities for a host of other sectors.

sections.label: Cushioning carbon tax impact
sections.summary: The Government should consider channelling part of carbon tax revenue to subsidise transition costs and green technology adoption, citing Sweden's phased implementation.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: To cushion the impact, the Government should consider channelling part of the carbon tax revenue to subsidise the increase in cost for a specific transition period, as well as provide subsidies to adopt green technologies to spur companies towards green practices and reduce use of energy.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: One good example is Sweden, which oversaw three decades of phased implementations before reaching its current pricings, without hemorrhaging economic developments.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: So, Sir, a clear long-term trajectory of the expected changes to carbon tax will be key to Singapore, to help companies make the business case to adopt new green technologies and make the necessary investment.

sections.label: Carbon offsetting as strategy
sections.summary: There is growing recognition that carbon offsetting may need to be part of the immediate strategy for transitioning to a low-carbon society.

sentences.speaker: Prof Koh Lian Pin (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: At the same time, there is growing recognition that carbon offsetting may need to be part of our immediate strategy as we transition to a low-carbon society.

sections.label: Southeast Asia carbon credit supply
sections.summary: At least 160 million hectares of investible, carbon-rich forests in Southeast Asia could supply some 400 million tonnes of nature-based carbon credits annually if protected as carbon projects.

sentences.speaker: Prof Koh Lian Pin (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In fact, there are at least 160 million hectares of investible, carbon-rich forests across Southeast Asia that could provide an annual supply of some 400 million tonnes of nature-based carbon credits, if they came under protection as carbon projects.

sections.label: Emerging Stronger Taskforce set up
sections.summary: In May 2020, Deputy Prime Minister Heng Swee Keat set up the Emerging Stronger Taskforce, led by Minister Desmond Lee and Mr Tan Chong Meng.

sentences.speaker: Prof Koh Lian Pin (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In May 2020, Deputy Prime Minister Heng Swee Keat set up the Emerging Stronger Taskforce (EST), led by Minister Desmond Lee and Mr Tan Chong Meng.

sections.label: Climate Impact X establishment
sections.summary: The AfA on Sustainability anticipated a trusted platform for carbon trading transparency, leading to Climate Impact X, a partnership between DBS, SGX, Standard Chartered and Temasek.

sentences.speaker: Prof Koh Lian Pin (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The AfA on Sustainability was prescient, in anticipating the need for a trusted platform, that would provide transparency in carbon trading for businesses to support nature-based carbon projects.

sentences.speaker: Prof Koh Lian Pin (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: This led to the establishment of Climate Impact X, a global exchange and marketplace for high-quality carbon credits, through a partnership between DBS, SGX, Standard Chartered and Temasek.

sections.label: Tension in low-carbon transition
sections.summary: Tension with societal priorities will likely remain, but reminds us that in the low-carbon transition, no one succeeds until everyone succeeds.

sentences.speaker: Prof Koh Lian Pin (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The tension between these and other societal priorities will likely remain.

sentences.speaker: Prof Koh Lian Pin (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: But this constant tension can be helpful in reminding us, that in our transition towards a low-carbon society, no one succeeds until everyone succeeds.

sections.label: Balanced approach to carbon pricing
sections.summary: With the impending revision of Singapore's carbon tax regime, the Government should adopt a balanced approach to carbon pricing with subsequent increases paced and tiered.

sentences.speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: As such, with the impending revision of Singapore’s carbon tax regime, the Government should adopt a balanced approach to carbon pricing with subsequent increases paced.

sentences.speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: While a higher carbon tax can drive reductions in carbon emitting activities, it is important that Carbon pricing be tiered to match against the greener alternatives available or abatement efforts.

sections.label: Relief for carbon tax effects
sections.summary: Carbon taxes can have regressive effects on vulnerable segments, so the Government should assure relief similar to GST increases.

sentences.speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: As carbon taxes can have regressive effects on the vulnerable segments of our society who spend a higher proportion of their income on basic services such as electricity bills, such negative effects need to be addressed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I hope that as a higher carbon tax is being contemplated, the Government can provide some assurance that relief will be granted in the same way we cushion for GST increases.

sections.label: Government help for carbon awareness
sections.summary: Shopkeepers and residents want to be green and know their carbon output, so Government can facilitate awareness programmes, carbon footprint calculators and alternatives.

sentences.speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Shopkeepers and residents in our neighbourhood want to be green and want to know how much carbon they produce.

sentences.speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: This is where Government can help facilitate through sharper awareness programmes, through providing carbon footprint calculators and alternatives to facilitate individual action.

sections.label: Loans for decarbonisation projects
sections.summary: Investors globally are willing to offer loans at favourable rates, and demand is set to increase as organisations finance decarbonisation efforts and projects.

sentences.speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Investors globally have demonstrated willingness to offer loans at favourable rates while demand is also set to increase as organisations look to also finance decarbonisation efforts and projects.

sections.label: Voluntary Carbon Market still nascent
sections.summary: Carbon credits have been recognised in the Kyoto Protocol since 1997, but the Voluntary Carbon Market is still at a nascent stage.

sentences.speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Even though carbon credits are recognised as part of the climate solution in the Kyoto Protocol since 1997, in reality, the Voluntary Carbon Market (VCM) is still at a nascent stage.

sections.label: Singapore exploring carbon schemes
sections.summary: The Government is exploring carbon schemes, including enabling large emitters to buy high quality international carbon credits to offset liabilities, with exchanges participating.

sentences.speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: As such, I am glad that the Government is exploring the use of carbon schemes such as the enablement of large carbon emitters in Singapore to purchase high quality international carbon credits to offset their liabilities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: With innovative solutions, Singapore-based international carbon exchanges can also participate in this transition which has other spin-off benefits like spurring greener projects such as R&D in clean hydrogen, developing carbon sinks and clean energy farms in the region.

sections.label: Singapore phasing out ICE vehicles
sections.summary: Singapore plans to phase out internal combustion engine vehicles by 2040 and replace them with electric vehicles.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Singapore plans to phase out internal combustion engine (ICE) vehicles by 2040 and replace them with electric vehicles.

sections.label: BEV charger study and rollout
sections.summary: A KBR study estimated about 164,000 publicly available BEV chargers are needed for a 100% BEV scenario, while Singapore plans 60,000 charging points by 2030.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: A study by KBR, commissioned by the National Climate Change Secretariat, estimated that approximately 164,000 publicly available BEV chargers will be required for a 100% BEV scenario.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Singapore plans to roll out just 60,000 BEV charging points by 2030.

sections.label: Cobalt price rise 2021
sections.summary: The price of cobalt rose by 90% between January and December 2021.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The price of cobalt rose by 90% between January and December 2021.

sections.label: Deloitte FCEV cost forecast
sections.summary: A Deloitte study forecasted that FCEV total cost of ownership will be less than BEVs by 2026.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Third, a study by Deloitte forecasted that the total cost of ownership of FCEVs will be less than BEVs by 2026.

sections.label: Hydrogen prices and suitable vehicles
sections.summary: Hydrogen prices are expected to decline over 40% in 10 years, and an NCCS-commissioned KBR study found taxis, buses and heavy goods vehicles well-suited for hydrogen fuel.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: With improvements in technology, hydrogen prices are expected to decline over 40% in the next 10 years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The KBR hydrogen study commissioned by the National Climate Change Secretariat (NCCS) found that taxis, buses and heavy goods vehicles are well-suited for hydrogen fuel, given the high daily distances they travel.

sections.label: Solar energy 2030 target
sections.summary: The Government is targeting a two gigawatt peak of solar energy by 2030.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The Government is targeting a two gigawatt peak of solar energy by 2030.

sections.label: Solar cost and private property owners
sections.summary: The Minister stated solar energy cost is now generally cheaper than retail electricity price and regulated tariff, making it economic to encourage solar PV installation among private property owners and buy their electricity.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The Minister also stated in his reply to Assoc Prof Lim that the cost of solar energy is now generally cheaper than the retail electricity price and regulated tariff.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: It would therefore make economic sense to encourage widespread installation of solar PV panels among private property owners and purchase electricity from them.

sections.label: Incentivising solar panel installation
sections.summary: Incentivising all to install solar panels could improve coverage and help Singapore derive more than the projected 4% of electricity from solar, with excess electricity transferred to the grid without payment until subsidies are covered.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Incentivising all of them to install solar panels could greatly improve our solar panel coverage.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: It could help Singapore derive more than the projected 4% of our electricity from solar energy.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: To clear, I am not suggesting that the Government should unconditionally subsidise landed property owners or companies to install solar panels, which they can later profit from by selling electricity back to the grid.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: They should be required to transfer excess electricity back to the grid without receiving any payments until their installation subsidy is fully covered.

sections.label: Push for FCEVs and solar
sections.summary: The speaker urges pushing harder on FCEV adoption, a bold hydrogen roadmap, and incentivising solar PV panel installation in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Let us push harder on the adoption of FCEVs, come up with a bold hydrogen roadmap and incentivise the installation of solar PV panels in Singapore.

sections.label: PAP Town Councils Green Towns initiative
sections.summary: 15 PAP Town Councils launched Action for Green Towns in May last year to level up community sustainability practices under the Green Plan.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: As part of the contributions made towards Singapore's goals under the Green Plan, 15 PAP Town Councils launched the Action for Green Towns (AGT) initiative in May last year to level up our sustainability practices within the communities.

sections.label: Paper recycling machines in HDB estates
sections.summary: The AGT taskforce partners with SGRecycle to deploy at least 78 paper recycling machines in HDB estates, with Marsiling-Yew Tee launching five.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: To achieve zero waste, the AGT taskforce is partnering up with SGRecycle to deploy at least 78 paper recycling machines in HDB estates.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: Marsiling-Yew Tee Town Council is one of the Town Councils taking part in this initiative and has since launched five machines across four divisions.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: We hope that this will improve recycling rates up to an estimated one to 1.5 tonnes of paper per machine per month, which is equivalent to saving 17 trees.

sections.label: Sustainability sector job creation
sections.summary: Minister Grace Fu shared in MSE's addendum that 55,000 jobs are expected in the sustainability sector over the next 10 years.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: As Minister Grace Fu has shared in the MSE's addendum to the President’s Address last year, 55,000 jobs are expected to be created in the sustainability sector over the next 10 years.

sections.label: Feed9B food sustainability platform
sections.summary: Feed9B is an open innovation platform bringing start-ups, SMEs, corporations, institutions and Government agencies together, and launched a Good Food Startup Manual.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: Aspiring entrepreneurs who wish to do so can tap on platforms, such as Feed9B, an open innovation platform that aims to bring start-ups, small medium enterprises (SMEs), large corporations, institutions and Government agencies together to promote food sustainability and innovation.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: Feed9B has also launched a Good Food Startup Manual, a free resource that helps entrepreneurs navigate the food landscape.

sections.label: Disinfectants from food waste
sections.summary: Food-grade, alcohol-free disinfectant products are made with ingredients that are 98% edible and derived from food waste such as cashew and soybean extracts.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: Their range of food-grade, alcohol-free disinfectant products are made with ingredients that are 98% edible and are derived from food waste, such as cashew and soybean extracts, which is a shining example of what our local startups are capable of in terms of promoting sustainability and green living.

sections.label: SkillsFuture workshops for green jobs
sections.summary: The speaker suggests the 5 CDCs organise more SkillsFuture workshops so Singaporeans, including vulnerable groups, can understand and be trained for green sector jobs.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: It is inspiring to see that, as we head towards these goals, we are also creating many new job opportunities in sustainable development sector.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: I suggest that the 5 CDCs organise more of these SkillsFuture workshops so that Singaporeans, regardless of age, including those vulnerable groups who are still seeking employment, can develop an interest in and understand job opportunities in the green sector and be trained with relevant skills.

sections.label: Corporate responsibility beyond Singapore borders
sections.summary: Corporate responsibility must consider external impact beyond Singapore, requiring incentives and regulations for thoughtful corporate practices.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Corporate responsibility cannot remain focused only on issues within our borders, but must consider the external impact that our industries' actions have beyond Singaporean shores.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: To do so, we must not only, as the Motion states, seek greater Government intervention to enhance corporate accountability, but we must also create the right set of incentives and regulations to build genuine, thoughtful corporate practices to maximise positive impact on our people, planet and prosperity.

sections.label: Olam Brazil labour allegations
sections.summary: Olam faced allegations in Brazil of child and slave labour in cocoa, and admitted it could not trace all cocoa beans.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: For example, Singapore-based Olam has found itself in hot water in Brazil recently.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: This issue was brought up by my Aljunied colleague Mr Leon Perera as allegations were made by the Brazil Federal Labour Prosecution Office and the International Labour Organization (ILO) that the company participated in the widespread use of child and slave labour in Brazil's cocoa industry.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: In filings last year, Olam admitted that they could not trace the origin of all their cocoa beans.

sections.label: Supply chain diligence and France law
sections.summary: Companies in Singapore should perform supply chain diligence, and France passed a 2017 law requiring vigilance plans for large companies.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: First, companies operating in Singapore should perform diligence on their supply chains and we need to proactively mitigate against any risks along the supply chain.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: In 2017, France passed a law that required companies above a certain size to establish a plan of vigilance for identifying risks of human rights, health and safety or environmental violations within their global supply chains.

sections.label: Assessing supply chain requirements for companies
sections.summary: Government should assess placing similar requirements on Singapore companies, perhaps starting with companies exceeding a certain size.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: As a high-income country, we should be ensuring our own suppliers are environmentally and socially sensitive to offer a competitive edge to those who source from other high-income countries who care about these considerations.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: It would thus be prudent for our Government to carefully assess whether similar requirements can be placed on companies that operate in Singapore, perhaps beginning with companies exceeding a certain size.

sections.label: Supporting AI and sensor tracking
sections.summary: Industries using AI and sensor tracking should be supported to help companies and governments exercise greater supply chain vigilance.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Third, we should continue to support industries that harness latest innovations from fields, such as artificial intelligence (AI) and sensor tracking, to allow companies and governments to exercise greater vigilance of supply chains.

sections.label: Sustainability awareness in education
sections.summary: Awareness of sustainability efforts must be built into the education system at all levels.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: First, awareness of our sustainability effort has to be built into our education system at all levels.

sections.label: Whistleblower protection and greenwashing
sections.summary: It calls for stronger whistleblower protection and consideration of frameworks tackling false and misleading practices, including greenwashing, to empower consumers.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Second, we must strengthen protection granted to whistleblowers to ensure that any violations have a higher chance of being found out and that a culture of corporate responsibility is better protected by workers and employers alike.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Frameworks or regulations that tackle false and misleading practices, including greenwashing, should also be considered to protect or empower consumers to flag out instances of greenwashing.

sections.label: Sustainability literacy of citizens
sections.summary: It states these measures will enhance citizens' sustainability literacy, enabling a more analytical and sceptical population willing to question false marketing.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: All these taken together will enhance the literacy and fluency of citizens in sustainability-related issues, enabling a more analytical and sceptical population who are willing to question and call out abuses of false marketing from companies.

sections.label: Green finance bodies and initiatives
sections.summary: It lists the Green Finance Industry Taskforce, MOF Green Bonds Programme Office, NEA Green Bond Framework, SGX sustainability reporting enhancements and green loans by financial institutions.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Some of these include the formation of the Green Finance Industry Taskforce, the MOF Green Bonds Programme Office and initiatives like the NEA Green Bond Framework, the recent SGX enhancements on sustainability reporting and climate-related disclosures, as well as the issuance of green loans by multiple financial institutions.

sections.label: Green finance and business support schemes
sections.summary: It states the MAS Green and Sustainability-Linked Loan Grant defrays green finance costs and the Enterprise Sustainability Programme supports Singaporean companies including SMEs.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: On a local level, schemes such as the MAS Green and Sustainability-Linked Loan Grant are useful in defraying the cost of accessing green finance.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: And for businesses which find it challenging to retrofit their operations to fulfil sustainability metrics, the Enterprise Sustainability Programme launched last year supports Singaporean companies, including SMEs, to build capabilities.

sections.label: Green Loan and Bond Catalogue
sections.summary: It states an MSE- or MAS-endorsed Green Loan and Bond Catalogue could help support businesses moving in the right direction.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Additionally, the creation of an MSE- or MAS-endorsed Green Loan and Bond Catalogue could be helpful in supporting businesses moving in the right direction.

sections.label: SGX climate disclosure mandate
sections.summary: It states SGX recently mandated issuers to provide climate-related disclosures by FY23 or FY24, depending on industry.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: SGX recently mandated issuers to provide climate-related disclosures by FY23 or FY24, depending on industry.

sections.label: Singaporean ESG reporting standard
sections.summary: MAS' Project Greenprint offers a common portal for ESG disclosures, but a Singaporean standard compatible with global standards would reduce compliance costs.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: There have been some efforts to somewhat synthesise these frameworks, such as MAS’ Project Greenprint providing a common portal to examine ESG disclosures across different international reporting frameworks.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: But it would be of greater clarity to work towards a strong, Singaporean standard, compatible with global standards for our businesses to aspire towards to reduce compliance costs.

sections.label: Sustainability Administration think tank
sections.summary: An autonomous Sustainability Administration policy-oriented think tank could be created as a Centre of Excellence for Sustainability Administration.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: One of the ways we can do this is through the creation of an autonomous Sustainability Administration policy-oriented think tank, as a Centre of Excellence for Sustainability Administration.

sections.label: MICE sustainability conventions
sections.summary: Singapore's MICE industry could host regular sustainability conventions and workshops to connect locals with top global talents.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: To further ride on these winds, we could also leverage upon Singapore’s (MICE) industry to host regular sustainability conventions and workshops to connect locals with top global talents.

sections.label: Green jobs and carbon trading
sections.summary: Singapore can create green collared jobs, transform industries regionally, and become Asia's trusted carbon trading hub to strengthen climate justice.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
sentences.text: But for the Singapore, beyond sacrifices, there are also opportunities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
sentences.text: I see great opportunity for Singapore to create numerous green collared jobs, not just for future graduates, but also matured PMETs, which is a rare opportunity that we can and must seize now.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
sentences.text: I see opportunities for Singapore, as the finance, governance and connectivity hub of the region, to transform and influence industries way beyond our shores, thereby cementing our regional hub status for one more generation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
sentences.text: I see opportunities for Singapore to strengthen climate justice by becoming the trusted carbon trading hub of Asia, by facilitating resource transfers from rich countries and consumers, to help those with less become more sustainable, thereby empowering all of us to save the world together.

sections.label: Loss and damage fund
sections.summary: The concept of the loss and damage fund is clearly on the agenda for COP27 in Egypt this year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
sentences.text: In fact, the concept of the “loss and damage fund” is now clearly in the agenda for COP27 in Egypt this year.

sections.label: Sustainable Finance and Carbon Hub
sections.summary: Singapore can shape rules and connect trading blocks and competing powers, transforming into the Sustainable Finance, Business and Trusted Carbon Trading Hub of Asia.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
sentences.text: Here lies the opportunity of Singapore to play a decisive role in the region, and even in the world, to shape the rules, to connect different trading blocks and competing powers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
sentences.text: And by doing so, we can transform Singapore into the Sustainable Finance, Business and Trusted Carbon Trading Hub of Asia.

sections.label: Encouraging use of Climate Impact X
sections.summary: Singapore-based companies can be encouraged to use the new Climate Impact X global carbon exchange launched by Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
sentences.text: Five, we can encourage Singapore-based companies to use the new Climate Impact X, the new global carbon exchange launched by Singapore.

sections.label: National utility, alliance and SkillsFuture roadmap
sections.summary: Proposals include a national utility for business sustainability, a Singapore alliance for sustainable finance and carbon trading, and a SkillsFuture roadmap for green collar jobs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
sentences.text: Six, we can put together a national utility for business sustainability, like how our TradeNet serves the import and export business.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
sentences.text: Seven, create a Singapore industry association or alliance specific for sustainable finance, business and carbon trading.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
sentences.text: This alliance can then help the Government to develop the industry.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
sentences.text: And finally, eight, create a solid SkillsFuture roadmap and position many Singaporeans for these green collar jobs.

sections.label: GFMA report on low carbon investment
sections.summary: A GFMA report states $100-150 trillion is needed over three decades for a low carbon transition, with $66 trillion needed in Asia.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: According to a Global Financial Markets Association (GFMA) report, the development of which I must say my firm was involved, some $100-150 trillion US dollars in investments is needed over the next three decades to transition to a low carbon economy.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: This translates to at least $3-5 trillion in investments per year – an increase of five to eight times from current levels.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: And $66 trillion of these investments will be needed right here in Asia.

sections.label: Current carbon tax signals intent
sections.summary: Singapore's current $5 per ton carbon tax is not enough to shift behaviour but has signalled intent.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: In Singapore, we know that the current $5 per ton carbon tax is not enough to shift behaviour but it has served to signal intent.

sections.label: Carbon border tax and global value chains
sections.summary: The carbon border tax has arrived and its impact will be felt through global value chains, possibly redefining competitive balance between nations.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: At the same time, we cannot afford to lapse into naval gazing.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: This space is rapidly evolving, The carbon border tax has arrived and the impact will be felt through global value chains, and could redefine the competitive balance between nations in many industries.

sections.label: Phased carbon tax and transition pathways
sections.summary: The Government must move on the carbon tax with phased implementation, and the financial sector and scientific community must help companies design sector specific transition pathways.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: The Government must move on the carbon tax, albeit with a phased implementation.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: The Government, the financial sector and the scientific community must help companies and industry associations to design sector specific transition pathways as part of their industry transformation maps and manage their transitions; not just give companies time to adjust but help them move faster and with higher productivity.

sections.label: Singapore green economy opportunity
sections.summary: Singapore could be to climate and sustainability what Silicon Valley is to technology if it fully embraces the new green economy.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: If we do not fully embrace the new green economy, we might fall behind.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: But if we do, then imagine this: Singapore could be, for climate and sustainability, what the Silicon Valley is, for technology.

sections.label: Environmental engineering employment rates
sections.summary: In the 2020 Graduate Employment Survey, NUS and NTU environmental engineering graduates had full-time employment rates of 63.2% and 58.5%.

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
sentences.text: In the 2020 Graduate Employment Survey, two of our largest IHLs, NUS and NTU, saw full-time employment rates of 63.2% and 58.5% respectively, for environmental engineering, one of the lowest rates amongst engineering graduates.

sections.label: UC Berkeley sustainability courses
sections.summary: At UC Berkeley, sustainability-focused or related courses make up almost 50% of undergraduate courses, with 20% fully focused on sustainability.

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
sentences.text: University of California (UC), Berkeley's sustainability-focused or related course offerings make up almost 50% of all undergraduate courses, with 20% fully focused on sustainability.

sections.label: Public-private sustainability collaborations
sections.summary: The ITE-Sembcorp Centre for Sustainable Solutions and the Singapore Green Finance Centre are two examples of public-private sector collaborations.

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
sentences.text: Two examples of such public-private sector collaborations are the ITE-Sembcorp Centre for Sustainable Solutions and the Singapore Green Finance Centre.

sections.label: UK iCAST research centre
sections.summary: iCAST in the UK is a research centre from university, government, investor and enterprise collaboration that gives industry R&D access and speeds products to market.

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
sentences.text: The Innovation Centre for Applied Sustainable Technologies also known as iCAST in the UK, is a research centre birthed from the collaboration of university researchers, the government, investors and local enterprises. iCAST provides industry accessibility to R&D and investors, and helps players expedite the product to market process.

sections.label: iCAST expansion beyond energy
sections.summary: iCAST is the expanded version of NTU and Enterprise Singapore's EcoLabs Centre of Innovation for Energy, including sectors beyond energy.

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
sentences.text: Aligning to our local context, iCAST is the expanded version of NTU and Enterprise Singapore's EcoLabs Centre of Innovation for Energy, but includes sectors beyond energy.

sections.label: Sustainability innovation competitions
sections.summary: The Liveability Challenge and CapitaLand Sustainability X Challenge are annual global competitions encouraging sustainability innovations and supporting new product development.

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
sentences.text: The Liveability Challenge by Temasek Foundation and CapitaLand Sustainability X Challenge are annual global competitions that encourage sustainability innovations and support them in another stage of new product development.

sections.label: Green skills in frameworks
sections.summary: The Government could study how local and overseas companies incorporate green processes, and integrate green competencies into SkillsFuture frameworks and leadership programmes.

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
sentences.text: The Government could further enable through studies on how local companies here as well as overseas have incorporated green processes to their work.

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
sentences.text: These practices and related competencies can be incorporated into our SkillsFuture Industry Skills Frameworks.

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
sentences.text: At the leadership level, green competencies, such as Sustainable Corporate Leadership Programmes that incorporate ESG factors, should be integrated into the "Leadership and People Management Framework".

sections.label: Carbon taxes and border adjustment
sections.summary: Taxes need a certain transparent price pattern, and Singapore may explore a carbon border adjustment mechanism to equalise carbon prices.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: One, to be effective in guiding behaviour, taxes must offer a certain and transparent price pattern so that businesses can project their potential expenses and plan accordingly.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Two, given that different countries may have different climate change standards and measures, Singapore may wish to eventually explore a carbon border adjustment mechanism to equalise the carbon prices of Singapore products and imported products from outside Singapore.

sections.label: Pacing carbon tax increases
sections.summary: While IMF economists suggest high-income economies aim for US$50 to US$75 per tonne by 2030, carbon tax increases must be paced so businesses can adapt.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Four, while IMF economists have suggested that high-income economies should aim for a carbon price of US$50 to US$75 per tonne of carbon dioxide emissions (tCO2e) by 2030, we must be careful to pace any increase in our carbon tax so that businesses can adapt and not be forced to leave Singapore.

sections.label: Global carbon credit demand
sections.summary: McKinsey estimates annual global carbon credit demand could reach 1.5 to 2.0 GtCO2 by 2030 and seven to 13 GtCO2 by 2050.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: According to estimates from McKinsey, the annual global demand for carbon credits could reach up to 1.5 to 2.0 gigatons of carbon dioxide (GtCO2) by 2030 and up to seven to 13 GtCO2 by 2050.

sections.label: Green skills job roles
sections.summary: The report highlighted that over 450 job roles in 17 sectors require green skills, including financial services, manufacturing, trade and connectivity, hospitality, and the built environment.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: The report highlighted that today, there are more than 450 job roles in 17 sectors that require green skills – including financial services, manufacturing, trade and connectivity, hospitality, and the built environment.

sections.label: UK low-carbon economy value
sections.summary: The UK low-carbon and renewable-energy economy was worth £46.7 billion in 2018, up 15% on 2015 levels.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: The low-carbon and renewable-energy economy in the UK was worth £46.7 billion in 2018, up 15% on 2015 levels.

sections.label: Green finance capacity workshops
sections.summary: The Green Finance Industry Taskforce announced workshops for financial institutions and corporates to build green finance capacity from May 2021 to April 2022.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: The Green Finance Industry Taskforce announced plans to launch workshops for financial institutions and corporates to build capacity in green finance from May 2021 to April 2022.

sections.label: Not curbing brown financing
sections.summary: The approach is not to directly curb financing of brown activity such as palm oil or coal, but to wait for greener alternatives to replace it.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Our approach has been one of not curbing directly the financing of brown activity, such as palm oil or coal-related activity, but one that is to wait for greener alternatives to replace it.

sections.label: Carbon tax with transformation support
sections.summary: A carbon tax is agreed in principle as necessary, but must be coupled with transformational support and plans for industries and workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: While I agree in principle that a carbon tax is necessary to measure the costs of carbon emissions and trigger positive changes, this must be coupled with transformational support and plans for industries and workers to further equip to go green.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: We need to calibrate the tax amount and couple this with a higher magnitude of transformation support.

sections.label: Software energy savings in buildings
sections.summary: Proven cases show software driven approaches have saved between 20% and 40% of energy consumption at a building or plant level.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Based on current industry advancements, there have been proven cases that such software driven approaches have saved between 20% and 40% of energy consumption at a building or plant level.

sections.label: Course graduates digital facility managers
sections.summary: Johnson Controls helps link course participants to building clients hiring digital facility managers, with three quarters of participants above age 45.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Upon graduation from the course, Johnson Controls supports and play a role in linking the participants to the network of building clients who are in need to hire digital facility managers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: It is also worthy to note that three quarter of the course participants are above the age of 45 who are mid-career professionals seeking new meaningful opportunities in the green economy.

sections.label: Green skills and partnerships
sections.summary: The passage calls for strengthening digital and traditional engineering skills and scaling private sector partnerships to help businesses go green and create purposeful jobs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Alongside such tax reforms, we need to: one, strengthen the nexus between digital and more traditional engineering skillsets; and two, strengthen and scale private sector partnerships in aligning new skills, new purposeful jobs and the expertise industries need to go green.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: These measures enable businesses to adopt the triple "P" bottom line framework.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: As more businesses succeed in going green, this will create a butterfly effect on the whole of society and lend a boost of faith to those who are hesitant towards green transformation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: I believe we can make going green a sooner and more viable option for our businesses and create new and purposeful jobs for Singaporeans.

sections.label: Singapore Green Plan 2030 launch
sections.summary: Singapore launched the Singapore Green Plan 2030, a whole-of-nation movement outlining plans for a more sustainable Singapore.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: As a responsible global citizen, Singapore must also play our part in making our world sustainable.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: We launched a whole-of-nation movement, the Singapore Green Plan 2030 last year, outlining our plans towards a more sustainable Singapore.

sections.label: Green economy pillar aims
sections.summary: Under the green economy pillar, Singapore aims to capture green growth, transform businesses to integrate sustainability, and equip workers with relevant skills.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: Under the green economy pillar of the Singapore Green Plan 2030, we aim to do three things; first, capture green growth opportunities; second, transform our existing businesses and industries to integrate sustainability into their business models; and third, equip our workers with relevant skills so that they can benefit from green growth.

sections.label: MAS green finance action plan
sections.summary: MAS developed a holistic green finance action plan to support sustainable finance, strengthen financial sector resilience and standardise climate-related disclosures.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: The Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS) has developed a holistic green finance action plan to support sustainable finance market development, strengthen the financial sector's resilience to environmental risks and standardise and enhance climate-related disclosures.

sections.label: Carbon services firms in Singapore
sections.summary: In 2021, 13 international firms anchored and expanded their carbon services offerings in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: In 2021, 13 international firms anchored and expanded their carbon services offerings in Singapore.

sections.label: Energy and chemicals sector targets
sections.summary: The aspiration is for the energy and chemicals sector to quadruple sustainable product output from 2019 levels and achieve over six million tonnes of annual carbon abatement by 2050.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: Our aspiration is for the energy and chemicals sector to increase its output of sustainable products by four times from 2019 levels and achieve more than six million tonnes of carbon abatement per annum from low-carbon solutions by 2050.

sections.label: Energy transition and solar deployment
sections.summary: MTI and EMA are decarbonising electricity, accelerating solar and planning to import up to four gigawatts by 2035, with no solar subsidies.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: MTI and the Energy Market Authority (EMA) are therefore embarking on energy transition plans to decarbonise electricity production.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: We are accelerating solar deployment and plan to import up to four gigawatts of electricity by 2035.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: Mr Gerald Giam asked about the subsidies for solar deployment, especially for the private property.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: We do not have subsidies for solar deployment as solar is already cheaper than our retail electricity and there is already incentive for them to do so.

sections.label: CCP clean energy job transition
sections.summary: Over two years the new CCP will support up to 150 existing employees and mid-careerists into clean and renewable energy-related jobs.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: Over the next two years, the new CCP will support the transition of up to 150 existing employees that are impacted and mid-careerists from other sectors into the clean and renewable energy-related jobs.

sections.label: Enterprise Sustainability Programme for businesses
sections.summary: The Enterprise Sustainability Programme, announced last October, is expected to benefit at least 6,000 enterprises over the next four years.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: Last October, I announced the Enterprise Sustainability Programme (ESP) to help local businesses build capabilities in sustainability and capture opportunities in a green economy.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: The ESP is expected to benefit at least 6,000 enterprises over the next four years.

sections.label: Australia GEA negotiations
sections.summary: Negotiations with Australia are underway for the first of these GEAs.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: Negotiations with Australia are underway for the first of these GEAs.

sections.label: Low-Carbon Energy Research funding awards
sections.summary: Last year $55 million was awarded to 12 projects under the Low-Carbon Energy Research Funding Initiative for hydrogen and CCUS technologies.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: For example, last year, we awarded $55 million to 12 projects under the Low-Carbon Energy Research Funding Initiative, which will see collaboration between research institutes and industry to develop low-carbon technologies, such as hydrogen and CCUS.

sections.label: Revisiting 2030 climate pledges
sections.summary: Parties agreed to revisit their 2030 climate pledges and communicate long-term low emissions strategies towards net zero, aligning with the Paris Agreement temperature goal.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: Parties agreed to revisit their 2030 climate pledges, or Nationally Determined Contributions (NDC) and communicate Long-term Low Emissions Development Strategies (LEDS) towards net zero emissions, to align with the Paris Agreement temperature goal.

sections.label: Article 6 carbon credit negotiations
sections.summary: Singapore and Norway co-facilitated negotiations that concluded the Article 6 rulebook, enabling transfer of emission reductions between countries.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: Singapore, together with Norway, co-facilitated negotiations that brought the Article 6 rulebook across the finishing line, after six years of protracted talks.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: The agreement on Article 6 clears the path for the establishment of mechanisms that facilitate the transfer of emission reductions, or carbon credits, we call it, between countries to meet their climate targets, while ensuring high standards of environmental integrity.

sections.label: Singapore joins coal phase-out alliance
sections.summary: Singapore became Asia's first country to join the Powering Past Coal Alliance, aiming to phase out unabated coal by 2050.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: Singapore became the first country in Asia to join the Powering Past Coal Alliance to progressively phase out the use of unabated coal in our electricity mix by 2050.

sections.label: GFANZ and Race To Zero membership
sections.summary: GFANZ has gathered over 450 financial institutions with assets above US$130 trillion, and over 5,000 companies joined the UN Race To Zero campaign.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: The Glasgow Financial Alliance for Net Zero (GFANZ) has gathered more than 450 financial institutions with assets in excess of US$130 trillion, in the common pursuit of aligning their investment portfolios with credible net zero pathways.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: More than 5,000 companies worldwide have now joined the UN Race To Zero campaign, pledging to take immediate action towards achieving net zero by mid-century, publish clear action plans and submit regular progress reports.

sections.label: IPCC sea level rise projection
sections.summary: The IPCC reports global mean sea level rise could reach up to one metre by 2100 under a high emissions scenario.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: The IPCC reports that global mean sea level rise could reach up to one metre by 2100, if the world pursues a high emissions scenario pathway.

sections.label: Multinationals low-carbon supplier plans
sections.summary: A Standard Chartered Bank study showed eight in 10 multinationals plan to work only with suppliers aligned with their low-carbon transition plans by 2025.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: A recent study by Standard Chartered Bank showed that eight in 10 multinationals plan to work exclusively with suppliers that are aligned with their low-carbon transition plans by 2025.

sections.label: Carbon tax emissions coverage
sections.summary: Singapore's carbon tax covers about 80% of total emissions, and including vehicular fuel excise duties, more than 90% are subject to a carbon price.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: Our carbon tax covers about 80% of our total emissions.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: If we include the excise duties on vehicular fuel, more than 90% of our emissions are subject to a carbon price.

sections.label: Spending to incentivise energy efficiency
sections.summary: For the first five years, Singapore is prepared to spend more than it collects to incentivise energy-efficient processes and abatement projects through REG(E) and E2F.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
