sentences.text: In fact, for the first five years, we are prepared to spend more than we collect, to incentivise the adoption of energy-efficient processes and other worthwhile abatement projects, such as through the enhanced Resource Efficiency Grant for Energy (REG(E)) and Energy Efficiency Fund (E2F).

sections.label: Budget 2022 review outcome
sections.summary: The Minister for Finance will announce the outcome of the review at Budget 2022.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: The Minister for Finance will announce the outcome of our review at Budget 2022.

sections.label: Carbon credits as complementary pathway
sections.summary: Carbon credits from emission reduction projects elsewhere give these companies a complementary pathway to greater near-term abatement while long-term fixes are developed.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: For these companies, the ability to tap on carbon credits from emission reduction projects elsewhere provides a complementary pathway to deliver greater abatement in the near term, while long-term fixes, such as changes to business models, production processes, are being developed and implemented.

sections.label: Uncertainty and carbon markets access
sections.summary: Uncertainty over technological maturity and transboundary cooperation means access to well-functioning carbon markets is a complementary option if domestic abatement options do not materialise.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: However, there is significant uncertainty associated with these options at the moment, given that their commercial success hinges on factors such as technological maturity and transboundary cooperation, which are not entirely within our control.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: Therefore, access to well-functioning carbon markets serves as a complementary option in our toolkit to meet our climate commitments, especially in the event that domestic abatement options do not materialise.

sections.label: Rules for environmental integrity
sections.summary: To address the trust deficit, robust rules and clear guidelines centred on environmental integrity are needed, which is why Singapore co-facilitated Article 6 discussions.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: To address this trust deficit, we must first establish robust rules and clear guidelines centred on environmental integrity, ensuring that the generation of carbon credits from emissions reductions projects achieves the desired outcomes of reducing overall global emissions.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: This is why Singapore agreed to co-facilitate discussions on Article 6 – to provide a common rules-based, global framework and a foundation to safeguard environmental integrity and avoid double-counting.

sections.label: SGX climate disclosure roadmap
sections.summary: SGX published in December 2021 its roadmap for mandatory climate-related financial disclosures for listed entities, starting with those most exposed to climatic risks.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: SGX has published in December 2021, its roadmap for mandatory climate-related financial disclosures for listed entities, starting with listed entities in industries that are most exposed to climatic risks.

sections.label: Green labelling and certification schemes
sections.summary: Singapore has home-grown schemes like the Singapore Green Labelling Scheme and BCA's Green Mark Certification Scheme to help consumers identify sustainable companies.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: Other home-grown efforts include the Singapore Green Labelling Scheme, administered by the Singapore Environment Council, supported by NEA, as well as the Green Mark Certification Scheme by BCA for the built environment.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: So, we do have several of these schemes to help consumers make up their mind, to help decipher which are the companies that have complied with sustainability requirements.

sections.label: Singapore's low-carbon transition plans
sections.summary: Singapore will advance its competitive position through global climate action, green economy research, green finance, and investing in people under the Green Plan.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: Just like we have always tackled challenges squarely as a nation, we will continue to apply the same determination to the low-carbon transition, turning adversity, crisis, challenges into opportunity.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: We will build on our own strengths and continue to advance Singapore's competitive position by: supporting global climate action as a trusted interlocutor at multilateral fora, such as the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC), International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO), International Maritime Organization (IMO) and the World Bank; advancing research, pioneering innovative solutions, and building new norms and standards for the green economy; promoting green finance, digitalisation, and low-carbon innovation, which are key enablers for the green transition; and investing in our people to thrive in the green economy.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: Under the Green Plan, the Government will continue our efforts to spur whole-of-society action and catalyse partnerships across the people, public and private sectors for sustainability.

sections.label: Carbon exchange and green finance hub
sections.summary: Members proposed developing Singapore as a regional carbon exchange and green finance hub, supported by more green bonds and tax exemptions.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San
sentences.text: Mr Don Wee, Mr Derrick Goh, Ms Mariam Jaafar, Mr Henry Kwek and Mr Gan Thiam Poh proposed to develop Singapore as the carbon exchange marketplace for the region and building on our carbon marketplace ImpactX.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San
sentences.text: Mr Liang Eng Hwa and Mr Gan Thiam Poh called for Singapore to be developed as a green finance hub of the region.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San
sentences.text: And to support this goal, more Government green bonds to finance sustainability projects should be issued and tax exemptions for green finance products should be extended to companies.

sections.label: Calls to increase carbon tax
sections.summary: Members called for a higher carbon tax to nudge firms towards sustainable practices, with a tiered regime where lower emitters pay less.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San
sentences.text: Mr Louis Ng, Ms Foo Mee Har, Mr Derrick Goh and Mr Saktiandi Supaat called for an increase in carbon tax so as to nudge firms towards more sustainable practices.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San
sentences.text: They also opined that a tiered carbon tax regime being fairer as companies with lower emissions will pay a lower rate.

sections.label: Green Action Community and Town programmes
sections.summary: MSE implemented the Green Action Community Plan and 15 PAP Town Councils started the Action for Green Town programme for greener towns.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San
sentences.text: MSE has recently implemented the Green Action Community Plan and the 15 PAP Town Councils have also started the Action for Green Town programme to make our towns greener, zero-waste and energy-efficient.

sections.label: Climate adaptation and economic strength
sections.summary: Works like Pulau Tekong polder construction are proceeding, and a strong economy and financial hub are needed to pay for climate mitigation infrastructure.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San
sentences.text: Will they be able to fulfil their pledges and follow up with implementation?

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San
sentences.text: We are already proceeding with works, such as the polder construction at Pulau Tekong and looking at other options to protect our coasts.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San
sentences.text: Another example worth monitoring will be the proposed floating city off the coast of Busan in South Korea, a UN-backed project, which is expected to have its first platforms up by 2025 .

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San
sentences.text: A strong economy is the prerequisite to a strong defence.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San
sentences.text: And we need to maintain our lead as a hub, especially as a financial centre, so that we can afford to pay for climate mitigation infrastructure.
